answer_1.quote: We consider two applications of open-ended text generation: 1) document continuation on WikiText-103 with articles fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia , and 2) story generation on WritingPrompts, which is a challenging task for inspiring continuations with abstract, highlevel story prompts submitted by online users and continuations responded by others freely on Reddit .

answer_2.quote: We adopt the following automatic metrics to evaluate generation quality: Repetition We use rep-n to measure sequence-level repetition according to the portion of duplicate n-grams . Diversity Following , we obtain an overall assessment of model repetition by considering repetition at different n-gram levels: MAUVE By computing information divergences in a quantized embedding space , MAUVE directly compares the learnt distribution from a text generation model to the distribution of human-written continuation. Coherence The semantic coherence between prefix and continuation is measured as the cosine similarity between their sentence embeddings represented by SimCSE .

answer_4.quote: Then, we ask 3 evaluators to compare generated continuations from Look-back and the second best baseline SimCTG in two dimensions: 1) fluency: diverse and natural content without repeated words, phrases or sentences; 2) coherence: well-organized and easy to follow; being consistent with the topics presented in the human-written prefix without abrupt topic drifts.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators choose one out of three options: the 1st continuation is better, the 2nd is better, or the two are of the same quality.
